title: Markets: Saturday 24 October

morning.session_note: Weekend edition · the week in review, with the week ahead
summary: US stocks posted a second weekly loss as doubts about AI spending hit tech: the S&P 500 fell 0.5% for the week and the Nasdaq 0.7%, including a 2.6% Nasdaq drop on Thursday after a batch of AI-related results, among them Meta's first cash outflow in more than a decade ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/nasdaq-futures-drop-over-1-as-ai-worries-resurface-oil-climbs-4965180), [Reuters via Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/wall-st-set-open-lower-130848087.html)). The US 10-year Treasury yield ended the week at 5.00%, 9 bp lower.

Brent futures settled at US$116.72 on Friday, the highest since 29 April and about 6% higher for the week, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, according to Reuters. On Friday President Trump said the US could end the war with Iran quickly but perhaps should let it wind down gradually ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/oil-little-changed-as-supply-concern-lingers-amid-houthi-attacks-on-saudi-arabia-4967907), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/23/oil-price-brent-wti-iran-war-saudi-arabia.html)). Moody's verdict on France's rating was not confirmed by our cutoff.

RBA Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said the inflation outlook is "materially worse", and ASX futures put the chance of a 3 November hike at 56% at Friday's close, up from 18% a week earlier ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://au.investing.com/news/economy-news/australian-central-banker-says-inflation-outlook-worse-unsure-about-november-rate-hike-4702859), [RBA Watch](https://rbawatch.com/rba-meeting/november-2026)). Next week brings Australian CPI on Wednesday and the Fed decision early Thursday Sydney time.

cards.headline: AI spending doubts gave US stocks a second weekly loss
cards.takeaway: Chip and big-tech shares led the falls and the pressure reached AI-linked debt, while energy shares hit a record.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Thursday's selloff was covered in the 23 Oct issue. Friday's session, the weekly totals and the AI-debt figures are new.
cards.what_happened: On Thursday the Nasdaq fell 2.6%, its steepest daily drop since early June, and the Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 6.7%, leaving it more than 26% below its 22 June record but still 51.5% up this year. Meta fell 7.0% after reporting its first cash outflow in more than a decade and a plan to issue non-voting shares; Intel, AMD, Sandisk and Marvell each fell more than 8% ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/nasdaq-futures-drop-over-1-as-ai-worries-resurface-oil-climbs-4965180)). On Friday the S&P 500 fell 0.52% and the Nasdaq 0.21%, and the Dow fell 1.23% but rose 0.4% for the week, its third straight weekly gain. The energy sector rose 2.5% to a record high and SLB rose 7% ([Reuters via Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/wall-st-set-open-lower-130848087.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: The selling has spread from AI shares to AI borrowers: CoreWeave's 2031 bond yielded 15.6% and its five-year credit default swap stood at 1,129 bp, above the 1,000 bp level usually treated as distressed ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/23/bonds-yields-us-treasurys.html)). Because these companies carry heavy index weights, Reuters' weekly preview said next week will be critical to whether third-quarter profits meet high expectations, with about a third of S&P 500 companies reporting ([Reuters Take Five via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/take-five-ai-trade-meets-the-fed-4968194)).
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: S&P 500 7,623.7 (−0.5% day, −0.5% week), Nasdaq 25,955.3 (−0.2% day, −0.7% week), VIX 19.58 (−0.41 points for the week).

competing_views.view: "Investors are starting to realize that there are some holes in the AI story."
"There is still fallout from the questioning of the AI trade," she said on Friday.

cards.what_to_watch: Alphabet and Microsoft report after the US close on Wednesday (Thursday morning Sydney time), and Amazon after the close on Thursday.

cards.headline: US firms raised prices at the fastest pace since 2022
cards.takeaway: Business activity cooled slightly in October, but firms' prices and households' inflation expectations both stayed high.
cards.key_figure: S&P Global flash output prices index: 59.8, highest since August 2022
cards.what_happened: The S&P Global flash composite PMI fell to 57.6 in October from a five-year high of 58.4, while the output prices index rose to 59.8 from 58.4 and new orders reached their highest since March 2022 ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/us-business-activity-cools-in-october-strong-demand-fueling-price-pressures-4969791)). Manufacturing came in at 56.0, a 53-month high, against a 55.3 estimate, according to CNBC. The University of Michigan sentiment index came in at 48.0, against a Dow Jones consensus of 46.3; year-ahead inflation expectations were 4.7% and long-run expectations 3.5% ([University of Michigan](https://www.sca.isr.umich.edu/), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/23/bonds-yields-us-treasurys.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: The Fed meets next week, and economists polled by Reuters expect it to hold and then raise rates again in December. S&P Global's Chris Williamson said supply bottlenecks and growing backlogs are "making it easier for companies to pass higher costs on to customers".
cards.what_to_watch: Advance Q3 GDP and September personal income and outlays, which include PCE inflation, are due at 8:30am US Eastern time on Thursday (11:30pm Thursday Sydney time).

cards.headline: ASX 200 ended flat for the week as Zip plunged
cards.takeaway: The index slipped 0.1% for the week; on Friday Zip fell 29.5%, miners fell and a business survey showed the private sector shrinking.
cards.what_happened: Zip Co fell 29.5% to A$1.46 on Friday, after dropping as much as 50.5% during the session, following its first-quarter update. Zip reported cash EBTDA of A$65.0 million, including A$10.1 million of US fraud costs, and reconfirmed its FY27 guidance ([Zip via ASX](https://www.asx.com.au/markets/trade-our-cash-market/announcements.zip), [IBTimes Australia](https://www.ibtimes.com.au/asx-200-falls-zip-shares-mining-stocks-1877239)). The S&P/ASX 200 materials index fell 3.9% on Friday and 7.7% for the week ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EAXMJ/)). Australia's flash composite PMI fell to 47.7 from 51.3, the first contraction in five months ([investingLive](https://investinglive.com/news/australia-flash-pmi-private-sector-shrinks-for-first-time-in-five-months-as-prices-rise/)).
cards.why_it_matters: The PMI showed activity shrinking while input costs rose at the fastest pace since May, according to investingLive. That combination is what the RBA weighs at its 3 November meeting, after Wednesday's CPI.
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: ASX 200 8,795.2 (+0.0% day, −0.1% week); AUD/USD 0.7006 at the RBA 4pm rate, +0.8% for the week. ASX 200 futures and iron ore are unavailable in our data.

cards.headline: Banks expect core inflation above the RBA's forecast in Wednesday's CPI
cards.takeaway: All four major banks forecast a trimmed mean above the RBA's 0.8%, but they are split on whether that brings a November hike.
cards.key_figure: Big four forecasts for Q3 trimmed mean: 0.9–1.0% q/q, against the RBA forecast of 0.8%
cards.new_since_last_issue: Hauser's comments were covered earlier in the week. The banks' CPI forecasts and calls are new.
cards.what_happened: Speaking on 21 October, Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said the inflation outlook was "materially worse" and that "we're in a world of hard choices", while declining to commit to a November move ([RBA](https://www.rba.gov.au/speeches/2026/sp-dg-2026-10-21.html), [Reuters via Investing.com](https://au.investing.com/news/economy-news/australian-central-banker-says-inflation-outlook-worse-unsure-about-november-rate-hike-4702859), [ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-10-21/reserve-bank-hauser-warns-inflation-outlook-materially-worse/107288574)). Unemployment rose to 4.7% in September, a five-year high, according to Reuters. CBA, NAB and ANZ forecast a 1.0% quarterly trimmed mean for the September quarter and Westpac 0.9%, with annual headline inflation of 3.9% and annual trimmed mean of 3.5–3.6% ([Savings.com.au](https://www.savings.com.au/news/stubborn-inflation-seen-ahead-of-key-rba-rates-decision)).
cards.why_it_matters: The RBA has raised rates four times this year, most recently three weeks before Hauser spoke, according to Reuters. Hauser framed the choice as tackling inflation or holding "our horses to protect the labour market", and the banks' split reflects that trade-off.

competing_views.view: Expect the RBA to raise rates again on 3 November.
Expect a hold. CBA's Belinda Saunders said much depends on the CPI and "the Governor's appearance before the Senate, both on Wednesday next week".

cards.what_to_watch: Q3 CPI and Governor Bullock's Senate appearance, both on Wednesday; Assistant Governor Sarah Hunter's 60 Minutes interview at 8:40pm Sunday.

cards.headline: Treasury yields fell for the week ahead of the Fed
cards.takeaway: The 10-year yield ended at 5.00% after briefly dipping below 5% for the first time in a month, and markets expect the Fed to hold next week.
cards.key_figure: US 10Y 5.00% (−9 bp week), US 2Y 4.69% (−5 bp week)
cards.what_happened: Yields rose about 5 bp on Friday, with the 10-year at 4.999% and the 2-year at 4.686%, after the 10-year fell below 5% on Thursday for the first time in a month as tech shares sold off. The Fed is expected to keep its 3.75–4.00% target range at next week's meeting, and CME FedWatch data showed about a 71% chance of a hike in December ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/23/bonds-yields-us-treasurys.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: Economists expect a hold next week and a hike in December, according to Reuters, so attention is on how Chair Kevin Warsh describes the outlook. PIMCO expects a pause with a tightening bias ([PIMCO](https://www.pimco.com/us/en/insights/october-fed-meeting-preview-a-pause-is-still-a-recalibration)).
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: US 10Y 5.00% (+4 bp day, −9 bp week), US 2Y 4.69% (+4 bp day, −5 bp week), US Treasury par yields; gold futures 4,010.7 (−4.1% week).

competing_views.view: "We don't expect Warsh to green light a December meeting rate hike."
Pointed to "two Fed rate hikes still built into expectations".

cards.what_to_watch: The Fed decision at 2pm US Eastern time on Wednesday (5am Thursday Sydney time) and the press conference after it.

cards.headline: Markets now lean towards an RBA hike on 3 November
cards.takeaway: The futures-implied chance of a hike tripled over the week, while 10-year bond yields edged lower.
cards.key_figure: November hike chance: 56% (23 Oct), from 18% (16 Oct)
cards.what_happened: ASX 30-day interbank futures implied a 56% chance of a 25 bp hike at Friday's close, with an expected rate of 4.74%. That was down from 62% on Thursday but up from 51% on Wednesday and 18% a week earlier ([RBA Watch](https://rbawatch.com/rba-meeting/november-2026)). On 21 October, Reuters reported markets pricing about a 40% chance, up from 30% at the start of that week ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://au.investing.com/news/economy-news/australian-central-banker-says-inflation-outlook-worse-unsure-about-november-rate-hike-4702859)).
cards.why_it_matters: With pricing close to even, Wednesday's CPI is likely to decide the market's view. A hike would take the cash rate from 4.60% to 4.85%.
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: AU 2Y 4.92% (±0 bp week); AU 10Y 5.28% (−4 bp week) as at 21 Oct, the latest RBA data; curve +36 bp.

cards.headline: Trump said the Iran war could end quickly or wind down gradually
cards.takeaway: Friday's comments came as Iran's army chief said Tehran is ready for "asymmetric warfare" and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia continued.
cards.new_since_last_issue: The strike-plan report, the IRGC warning and the Saudi attacks were covered on 23 Oct. Trump's Friday remarks and the Tasnim statement are new.
cards.what_happened: On Friday President Trump said the US could end the war with Iran quickly but perhaps should let it gradually wind down ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/oil-little-changed-as-supply-concern-lingers-amid-houthi-attacks-on-saudi-arabia-4967907)). Iran's army chief said Tehran is prepared for "asymmetric warfare", according to state agency Tasnim ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/23/oil-price-brent-wti-iran-war-saudi-arabia.html)). Earlier in the week, US officials told the New York Times that the US and Israel have plans for renewed strikes on Iran after the midterm elections ([New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/21/us/politics/us-israel-renewed-iran-strikes.html)). Trump said on Wednesday the US was not negotiating with Iran and something would happen "fairly soon" ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/23/oil-price-brent-wti-iran-war-saudi-arabia.html)), and the IRGC warned the conflict "will extend" to US bases if naval escorts continue, according to AFP ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/23/oil-price-brent-wti-iran-war-saudi-arabia.html), [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/live-news/us-iran-war-strait-hormuz-oil-prices-10-22-26)). Houthi attacks killed two people at Dammam airport and two at the Shaybah oil field, Saudi Aramco told staff to leave its Dhahran headquarters, and the State Department ordered non-essential staff out of Saudi Arabia ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/23/oil-price-brent-wti-iran-war-saudi-arabia.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: The market link is oil supply. Attacks on Saudi Arabia put the largest crude exporter's infrastructure at risk, and mixed signals from Washington on whether strikes resume leave the supply outlook uncertain into November. Andrew Lipow of Lipow Oil Associates said more oil has been moving out of Hormuz but "that could change at any minute" ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/oil-little-changed-as-supply-concern-lingers-amid-houthi-attacks-on-saudi-arabia-4967907)).

competing_views.view: Said "more oil came out of the Hormuz Strait over the last week than at any time previous", and posted that Iran is trying to drive up oil prices before the midterms.
Warned, via AFP, that the conflict "will extend" to US bases in the region if escorts of ships continue.

cards.what_to_watch: Any change in US military posture before 3 November, Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites, and Israel's election on Tuesday.

cards.headline: Brent posted a third weekly gain, to a six-month high
cards.takeaway: Brent settled at US$116.72 on Friday, up about 6% for the week, though our futures feed shows a lower price that we could not reconcile.
cards.key_figure: Brent settle US$116.72 (+3.1% Fri), highest since 29 April
cards.what_happened: Brent futures settled up US$3.55, or 3.14%, at US$116.72 and WTI rose 3.8% to US$103.27. Reuters put Brent's weekly gain at 6% and CNBC at 6.2%, its third straight weekly rise ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/oil-little-changed-as-supply-concern-lingers-amid-houthi-attacks-on-saudi-arabia-4967907), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/23/oil-price-brent-wti-iran-war-saudi-arabia.html)). The US Department of Energy authorised an exchange of up to 400,000 barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve for a supply disruption at Phillips 66's Lake Charles refinery, and Germany's stockpiling agency EBV issued a tender to sell from strategic reserves, its first since the G7 agreed to releases ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/oil-little-changed-as-supply-concern-lingers-amid-houthi-attacks-on-saudi-arabia-4967907)).
cards.why_it_matters: Buffers are thin. The US reserve holds 283 million barrels, the lowest since 1982 according to Department of Energy data cited by Al Jazeera, and the IEA says diesel is nearly double the price of crude ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/23/are-global-oil-reserves-sufficient-to-withstand-renewed-us-iran-war)). Fuel costs are part of the CPI and PCE readings due next week.
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: Brent futures 111.68 (−1.3% day, +1.7% week; Yahoo feed, see comparison below); Brent spot 115.22 as at 20 Oct (FRED, lagged); gold futures 4,010.7 (−1.2% day, −4.1% week).

competing_views.view: Discussing reserves against a wider supply shock: "A month or two is all we have," and "One hundred fifty dollars [per barrel] becomes a very distinct possibility".
Said "fears of supply disruptions" drove Friday's rise after a series of Houthi attacks across Saudi Arabia, including on energy infrastructure.

cards.headline: Ukraine's refinery strikes keep Russian diesel exports low
cards.takeaway: The first Russian diesel cargo under Trump's deal with Putin has sailed for New York, but analysts expect little effect on prices.
cards.key_figure: Russian diesel exports: 141,000 b/d in September, from 608,000 a year earlier (Kpler)
cards.what_happened: Ukrainian drone strikes on refineries cut Russia's diesel exports by more than 75% in September, according to Kpler data, and more than 1,000 drones targeted Russia on Sunday, according to Russian state media ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/21/ukraine-russia-drone-diesel-refinery-trump-putin-zelenskyy.html)). Under the deal Trump struck with Putin, Russia agreed to export about 75,000 b/d in October and 124,000 b/d in November. A tanker carrying 298,000 barrels of diesel left Primorsk for New York on Friday, due on 10 November, after Trump eased and then waived further sanctions on Russia ([NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/business/energy/russian-diesel-tanker-heads-us-trump-deal-putin-ukraine-war-rcna605187)).
cards.why_it_matters: Diesel moves freight and farm costs, so it feeds inflation more widely than petrol. The US average was US$6.32 a gallon, about 75% above a year earlier according to AAA, and Kpler estimates global diesel exports are down about 1 million b/d because of lost Russian and Middle East supply ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/21/ukraine-russia-drone-diesel-refinery-trump-putin-zelenskyy.html)).

competing_views.view: "It seems unlikely that they'll be able to bring the volume of diesel back to the market that they are talking about without an energy ceasefire."
Said the first tanker had departed and "further shipments will continue on a regular basis".

cards.headline: Moody's verdict on France was not confirmed by our cutoff
cards.takeaway: Most analysts expected Moody's to cut its Aa3 rating, after French 10-year yields hit their highest since 2002.
cards.key_figure: Moody's rating: Aa3, negative outlook, before Friday's scheduled review
cards.new_since_last_issue: The record spread was covered on 23 Oct. Analysts' expectations for the Moody's decision and Il Sole's funding figures are new.
cards.what_happened: On 22 October the French 10-year yield reached 5.142%, the highest since 2002, and its spread over German Bunds widened to 177 bp, a level not seen since 2011, according to Il Sole 24 Ore. Moody's decision was due after 2000 GMT on Friday, and most analysts expected a cut from Aa3, Reuters reported ([Il Sole 24 Ore](https://en.ilsole24ore.com/art/france-heres-whats-behind-the-flight-from-government-bonds-in-paris-AJWUFrrB), [Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/unresthit-france-poised-for-moodys-ratings-verdict-4968793)). S&P Global and Fitch already rate France A+ ([Agence France Trésor](https://www.aft.gouv.fr/en/frances-credit-ratings)). We found no published outcome by 7:30am Sydney time.
cards.why_it_matters: France plans about €340 billion of gross bond issuance next year, with non-residents holding 59.7% of its tradable debt, so wider spreads raise refinancing costs and can spill into other euro-area bond markets ([Il Sole 24 Ore](https://en.ilsole24ore.com/art/france-heres-whats-behind-the-flight-from-government-bonds-in-paris-AJWUFrrB)).

competing_views.view: Said a downgrade is largely priced in, so attention turns to Moody's outlook and how the story evolves before April's presidential election.

competing_views.who: Mike Bell, RBC BlueBay Asset Management
competing_views.view: Said pressure could grow if all three agencies cut France to BBB after the election, forcing sales by investors with rating limits: "That's where it could really start to get more ugly."

cards.what_to_watch: Moody's announcement and Monday's bond market reaction; the ECB decision on Thursday, where questions on French spreads are expected.
